name: Scopus (web)
description: Elsevier's abstract and citation database of peer-reviewed journals, books and conference papers in all fields.
coverage: About 100 million records from 30,000 active journals, books and conferences; social sciences, health, life and physical sciences; strong from 1996.
terms: Manual. For when you have Scopus through your library's website but no API key: Key writes the search in Scopus syntax and opens the site in its browser; you export the results and import the file.

steps: Sign in to Scopus through your library (Key opens the advanced search page).
Paste the search Key copied for you into the advanced search box and run it.
Set your years with the year range limiter on the results page.
Select all results, choose Export, pick RIS, include 'Citation information' and 'Abstract & keywords', and save the file. Scopus exports up to 20,000 records at a time.
Write down the number of hits and the date for your search log.
manual.importHint: Save the export file, then drag it onto Key's library or choose File, Import. Key reads RIS, BibTeX and CSV files and merges duplicates with what you already have.

guide.summary: Scopus is a large subscription database of peer-reviewed literature in all fields, run by Elsevier. Many systematic reviews search it next to PubMed because it covers social-science, economics and engineering journals that PubMed does not.
guide.coverage: About 100 million records from more than 30,000 journals, plus books and conference papers. Best from 1996; older records have fewer abstracts and references.
guide.fields: Title and abstract uses Scopus's TITLE-ABS-KEY field, which also searches author and index keywords. Subject searches the controlled index terms (such as MeSH or Emtree). Journal searches the source title. Identifier matches a DOI. The Standard detail level returns the first author only and no abstract; Complete returns every author, the abstract and keywords, but needs your institution's subscription (campus network or institutional token).
limits: Needs a Scopus subscription at your institution. Off campus, searches fail unless your library gives you an institutional token.
Proximity uses Scopus's W/n operator between the words of a term.
guide.credentials: Your library's subscription and sign-in. No API key is needed.
tips: Check the number of hits with the estimate before you run a large search, so you do not spend the weekly quota by accident.
If you only have web access to Scopus, use the Scopus (web) connector: Key writes the search for you and imports the exported file.
